after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A boat travels downstream on a river. The table below gives the speed $v(t)$, in miles per hour, of the boat at certain moments during its journey.

| $t\text{ (hours)}$ | $0$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ | $1$ | $1.3$ | $1.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v\text{ (mi/hour) }$ | $32$ | $35$ | $40$ | $65$ | $80$ | $65$ |

 Use the right Riemann sum for $v(t)$ over $[0,1.5]$ with five subintervals to approximate the total distance traveled by the boat.

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the speed-time graph.*
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ denote the area under the curve $y=v(t)$ over $[0,1.5].$ 
In this case, we have $n=5$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the total distance traveled can be approximated as

$$
A≈v(0.3)Δ{t}_{1}+v(0.7)Δ{t}_{2}+v(1)Δ{t}_{3}+v(1.3)Δ{t}_{4}+v(1.5)Δ{t}_{5},
$$

where each $Δ{t}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $t$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{t}_{i}={t}_{i}-{t}_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δt$'s.

| $t$ | $0$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ | $1$ | $1.3$ | $1.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δt$ | $-$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.3$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |
| $v(t)$ | $-$ | $35$ | $40$ | $65$ | $80$ | $65$ |

We plug in the numbers to approximate the number of liters and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈35\cdot 0.3+40\cdot 0.4+65\cdot 0.3+80\cdot 0.3+65\cdot 0.2 \\  & =10.5+16+19.5+24+13 \\  & =83.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total distance traveled by the boat. So, the distance is approximately $83\,\text{mi}.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
The table below gives some values of a continuous function $f(x)$ on the closed interval $[-6,3].$ The right Riemann sum approximation to the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ with $3$ equal subintervals has a value of $6.$ What must be the value of $k?$

| $x$ | $-6$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $7$ | $5$ | $-2$ | $k$ |
after.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the graph can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f(-3)+f(0)+f(3)}})\cdot {{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

Let's set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each point:

| $x$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $5$ | $-2$ | $k$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(5+(-2)+k)\cdot 3 \\  & =(k+3)\cdot 3 \\  & =3k+9\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are given that $A$ must be $6$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3k+9 & =6 \\ 3k & =6-9 \\ k & =\frac{-3}{3} \\ k & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The following table shows the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[10,16].$

| $x$ | $10$ | $12$ | $13.5$ | $16$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $7$ | $2$ | $4$ | $3$ |

Use the right Riemann sum, with the three subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area $A$ under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[10,16].$ 

$A≈$
{{field-1}}
after.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=3$ rectangles. Using the right Riemann sum, the area is approximated as 

$$
A≈f(12)Δ{x}_{1}+f(13.5)Δ{x}_{2}+f(16)Δ{x}_{3},
$$

where each $Δ{x}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the previous one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δx$'s.

| $x$ | $10$ | $12$ | $13.5$ | $16$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δx$ | $-$ | $2$ | $1.5$ | $2.5$ |
| $f(x)$ | $-$ | $2$ | $4$ | $3$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈2\cdot 2+4\cdot 1.5+3\cdot 2.5 \\  & =4+6+7.5 \\  & =17.5.\end{aligned}
$$
